topic: fixed linear Fourier thermal reciprocity and transient nonreciprocity interface audit
verdict: conditional theorem proved; 2025 article cannot be classified at exact source/receiver interface from indexed material

claims.claim: For fixed linear Fourier diffusion with positive volumetric heat capacity, symmetric positive conductivity, symmetric fixed Robin/Dirichlet/Neumann environment, and matched body-power source/weighted-temperature readout profiles, H_ij(s)=<b_i,(K+sC)^-1 b_j>=H_ji(s) for Re(s)>0.
claims.evidence: Symmetric weak form a_s(u,v)=a(u,v)+s m(u,v); reciprocity follows by swapping its two arguments.
limits: No advection, nonsymmetric conductivity, nonlinear or time-varying operator, powered feedback, or nonconjugate profile/output pairing.
Boundary-port Dirichlet-to-Neumann and Neumann-to-temperature versions require the appropriate paired boundary functionals and cannot be conflated with fixed homogeneous boundary data.

claims.claim: Initial-temperature Green kernels obey eta(x)G_T(x,y,t)=eta(y)G_T(y,x,t); equal initial temperature jumps can look asymmetric when heat capacities differ, while equal energy impulses give symmetric responses.
The 2022 primary paper defines two-terminal reciprocity by swapping boundary temperatures and requiring cross-paired time-averaged terminal heat fluxes to reverse sign (published Eq. 4).
claims.evidence: Li et al., Nat Commun 13, 167 (2022), DOI 10.1038/s41467-021-27903-3. This is a direct terminal-observable prior under the paper's mass-conserving time-modulated harmonic-steady-state assumptions, not the exact all-time fixed-LTI body-source theorem.

claims.claim: The 2015 transformation-thermotics diode uses explicitly temperature-dependent conductivity/geometry switches and reports rectification up to 30 for a numerical parameter set.
claims.evidence: Li et al., PRL 115, 195503 (2015), arXiv:1505.00971, Eqs. 2-4; therefore outside a fixed linear operator.

claims.claim: The 2017 two-slab transient rectifier relies on nonlinear temperature-dependent conductivity or thermal capacitance; transient rectification can exceed steady-state behavior under some conditions.
claims.evidence: Herrera, Luo & Go, J Heat Transfer 139, 091301 (2017), DOI 10.1115/1.4036339. A later primary article reports hot-boundary-temperature impulse from uniform cold initial state and linearized k(T); publisher PDF blocked in this audit.

claims.claim: The exact source, receiver, normalization, observable, and equation defining nonreciprocity in Su et al. (2025) are unknown from the accessible indexed material; no source-definition error can be asserted.
claims.evidence: Su et al., Int J Heat Mass Transfer 239, 126570 (2025), DOI 10.1016/j.ijheatmasstransfer.2024.126570. Indexed record mentions Dirac heat source/Green function, swapped source/receiver framing, transient spatial asymmetry and steady symmetry; full text inaccessible (403).

counterexample.description: Equal initial temperature impulses are not unweighted reciprocal when C varies.
counterexample.interpretation: The 4:1 asymmetry is the unequal energy of equal-Delta-T jumps, not a violation of matched-port reciprocity.

discriminating_experiment: At one fixed sample and geometry, compare same-joule localized source pulses with paired temperature readouts, then repeat with equal initial Delta-T and with swapped Dirichlet terminal temperatures/conjugate flux readout. Record source energy, temperature field, terminal fluxes, initial state, contact/ambient losses, source shape, actuator energy. Equal-Delta-T-only asymmetry is predicted by unequal capacity; a reproducible inequality under normalized matched power/temperature or boundary temperature/flux ports would challenge the fixed reciprocal model.
costs: Two directional runs per port pair; calibrated power, temperature and heat-flux sensing; baseline reset; calorimetric accounting; source-profile calibration; model fitting. No numeric costs available.
